data.body:
BRAINSTORM_IN_PROGRESS — paused 2026-05-01

This /dso:brainstorm session reached Step 4 (Fidelity Review) of the scrutiny pipeline before
pausing on a FEASIBILITY_GAP requiring multi-machine spike work that cannot be executed in
the brainstorm session itself. Captured below is the full state needed to resume.

## Approach (selected: Option A — Full Protocol with Same-Env Fast Path)

Two-tier claim fields on tickets (epic + terminal-leaf) with parent-pointer CAS via Epic 1
primitives. On CAS failure, sessions re-fetch and re-evaluate claim eligibility before
retrying or abandoning dispatch — never blind retry. Three-phase release-request protocol
(polite/urgent/final) as typed events on the tickets branch; release or decline allowed at
phases 1 and 2; phase 3 is a force-take notification. Phase 2 (urgent) hard blocking applies
at PostToolUse on Agent return as well as PreToolUse, so an orchestrator blocked in a
foreground Agent call sees the injection at its first tool boundary after Agent returns.
Force-take is independently gated on adaptive timeout by evidence tier (10/20/inf min).
Same-environment force-take is immediate when holder PID is verifiably gone; cross-environment
always uses three-phase escalation. Sub-agents emit CHECKPOINT and WORKTREE_* events directly
to the tickets branch from inside their worktree (not via the orchestrator), so evidence-tier
freshness is maintained during long foreground Agent blocks. PostToolUse hooks on ticket and
git operations walk the parent-chain hierarchy and inject unread events as system-reminders,
advancing per-event-class read cursors only on success (exit-144-safe). Worktree lifecycle
elevated from comments to typed events with monotonic seq numbers serving as fencing tokens.
Each force-release advances the claim's monotonic sequence number; the reducer rejects
subsequent CHECKPOINT, WORKTREE_*, or CLAIM_RENEWED events carrying a stale sequence number
AND surfaces an INVALIDATION signal to the writing session so sub-agents abort cleanly.
Reducer enforces total ordering by sequence number for all claim-state events. Lock-delay
(60s same-env, 5 min cross-env) after force-release widens the safety window. Resume scans
distinguish self-held from other-held claims; only act on self-held branches. Leaf claim
acquisition validates that the parent epic claim exists at write time. TTL = 30 min;
renewal target = 8 min, with sub-agent CHECKPOINT events providing passive freshness. Config
validation: evidence_timeout_cross_env > 2 × renewal_target; phase escalation intervals have
defaults in dso-config.conf. All Epic 2 events stay agent-internal; the Jira bridge allowlist
excludes them. Deployment ordering: bridge allowlist update precedes Epic 2 event-emitting
code; advisory quiescence at cutover (no in-flight orchestrator sessions, debug-everything
runs, or sprint batches when deploying).

## Success Criteria (current draft — needs Value+Scope reviewer fixes before approval)

1. A second orchestrator session attempting to claim an epic already held sees holder identity,
   claim age, and is presented with options (wait, pick alternative epic, initiate three-phase
   release request) — never silent collision.
2. Two sub-agents within a batch cannot start work on the same task: orchestrator's leaf-tier
   claim acquisition is atomic via parent-pointer CAS and the second dispatch attempt observes
   the claim and is not launched.
3. A zombie session's claim is automatically released within evidence-tier bounds (same-env
   immediate when PID gone; cross-env >20 min silence). Responsive holder declining requests
   retains the claim. A previous holder whose claim has been force-released receives an
   INVALIDATION signal; in-flight sub-agents abort cleanly rather than continue with stale-seq
   writes that the reducer would silently drop.
4. Blackboard, write-blackboard.sh, lock subcommands in agent-batch-lifecycle.sh, and
   release-debug-lock.sh removed. /dso:debug-everything no longer locks the session — two debug
   sessions on the same machine can run concurrently on disjoint bugs.
5. Worktree lifecycle as typed events (WORKTREE_START/COMPLETE/LANDED) with monotonic seq;
   worktree-tracking-comment.md deleted (hard cutover).
6. /dso:sprint, /dso:debug-everything, /dso:fix-bug SKILL.md guidance documents the claim
   lifecycle (acquisition at phase entry, renewal during long-running work, release on
   exit/closure, resume-scan replacing the WORKTREE_TRACKING comment scan with a typed-event +
   claim scan that distinguishes self-held from other-held claims).
7. Epic 2 events excluded from Jira bridge allowlist; bridge cannot loop them back inbound;
   bridge unit tests verify rejection of each new event type.

## Decisions Made (gap-question answers)

- Claim model: sibling field with own CAS (not assignee overload).
- Tiers: epic + terminal-leaf only. Stories with children are claimable but claim is meaningless.
- Tier protocol: same-env vs cross-env split — same-env immediate force-take when PID gone;
  cross-env always uses three-phase escalation.
- Bridge visibility: NONE of Epic 2 event types bridged to Jira ("no LLM noise" — option a).
- Decline semantics: release-or-decline allowed at BOTH polite AND urgent phases; phase 3
  force-take is notification not question. Force-take gated on evidence-tier silence,
  independent of phase escalation. Responsive declining holder retains claim indefinitely.
- Phase 2 enforcement scope: ALL tool calls blocked until release-or-decline emitted (option a).
- Renewal cadence: TTL=30 min, target=8 min; sub-agent CHECKPOINT provides passive freshness
  during foreground Agent blocks (with ratio TTL:renewal ≈ 3.75:1, matches etcd/Consul norms).
- Lock-delay: 60s same-env, 5 min cross-env (revised after scenario analysis flagged clock skew).
- Push mechanism split: tickets handle cross-env communication; messages (Epic 2b) handle
  in-env only. Cross-env messaging is OUT OF SCOPE.
- Sub-agent → orchestrator pattern: terminate-and-escalate (sub-agent writes structured
  request file + exits, SubagentStop hook normalizes, orchestrator processes, SendMessage
  resumes). Patterns from research: LangGraph interrupt/resume, OpenAI Swarm handoffs,
  GitHub Actions step output. Orchestrator → sub-agent: SendMessage to live agent.
- Worktree-tracking comment deprecation: hard cutover (single release).
- /dso:fix-bug claim integration: covered generically by SC #6 (skill guidance docs claim
  lifecycle for sprint, debug-everything, fix-bug).

## Architectural Splits — Follow-on Epics (NOT YET FILED)

These were planned to be filed in Phase 3 but are deferred until Epic 2 brainstorm completes:

1. Epic 2b (agent-addressed messaging): blocked by Epic 2; deliverables include
   USER_INPUT_REQUEST/RESPONSE, SUBAGENT_LAUNCH_REQUEST/RESULT, PREEMPT_REQUEST/ACK with
   sender/recipient model and request_id correlation. Single-environment scope (no cross-env).
   Unblocks bot-psychologist + fix-bug as sub-agents.
2. Rolling sprint/debug-everything batch replacement: blocked by Epic 2b; replaces the current
   batch process with a rolling process that's more efficient.
3. RATE_LIMIT propagation across coordinated sessions: blocked by Epic 2.

## Cross-Epic Interaction Scan (5 batches × 20 epics, 99 candidates)

Real conflict (deferred to its own re-brainstorm via comment posted on 4c54-4205):
- 4c54-4205 (Interface contracts for parallel agent and multi-session coordination):
  proposes blackboard extension; Epic 2 removes blackboard. 4c54 must be reformulated to use
  non-blackboard storage (typed events on tickets branch, .claude/contracts/, or ticket comments).

Considerations (handled via Cross-Epic Interactions section in spec):
- e884-d0ad (PostToolUse forced next-step): hook coexistence with priority documentation
- cda8-38b5 / 1d4f-9feb / 1de7-50d4 / 83e2-04ae (Jira bridge): allowlist composition
- cfb3-3f53 (compaction): preserve new event types in SNAPSHOTs
- e407-d35c (source attribution): coordinate ticket schema field naming
- a154-98de (PRECONDITIONS degradation): sprint Step 10a sequencing
- 70f6-05f1 (Clash file conflict): claim acquired before Clash check; Clash failure releases claim
- 71df-5bd8 (kudos snapshot): WORKTREE_START seq captured by kudos baseline
- 371f-cfc3 (external distribution): sequenced after Epic 2 closure or two-version handling
- a524-fded (test execution migration): shared _derive_session_id() helper
- 4e55-a6ba (PR-merge mode): consumes typed WORKTREE_LANDED post-cutover

Benign (logged, no action):
- ed62-08cd (cross-runner): Epic 2 events are JSON, language-agnostic
- c183-ed2a (session_id format): coordinated via shared helper

## Scenario Analysis (14 surviving from blue team, of 16 red-team scenarios)

Critical (3):
- CAS lost-update window during concurrent claim acquisition → mitigation: re-fetch + re-evaluate, never blind retry (added to approach)
- Monotonic seq rejection silently drops CHECKPOINT events → mitigation: INVALIDATION signal to writing session, sub-agents check + self-terminate (added to SC #3 + approach)
- Phase 2 urgent injection deadlock during foreground Agent block → mitigation: enforcement at PostToolUse on Agent-return as well (added to approach)

High (8):
- Lock-delay vs cross-env clock skew → tiered (60s/5min)
- Evidence-silence timeout during legitimate Agent block → sub-agent direct event emission to tickets branch
- CLAIM_RENEWED vs force-take race → reducer total ordering by seq
- Resume-scan self vs other claim → distinguish self-held vs other-held
- Hard cutover orphans WORKTREE_TRACKING comments in-flight → advisory quiescence at cutover
- Bridge allowlist deployment ordering → bridge update precedes Epic 2 event code
- Blackboard removal breaks in-flight debug → quiescence at cutover
- evidence_timeout_cross_env < renewal_target → config validation: evidence_timeout > 2×renewal_target
- Phase escalation interval defaults → defaults in dso-config.conf

Medium (3):
- PostToolUse hook latency under load → cursor-based incremental, time-bound execution
- Leaf-claim without parent epic → leaf CAS validates parent claim exists

Filtered (2):
- TTL clock skew (duplicate of lock-delay scenario)
- max_agents=0 with claim acquired (implementation choice)

## Fidelity Review Outcomes

- Agent Clarity: PASS (self_contained 4, success_measurable 5)
- Scope: FAIL — consumer_completeness 3. Wants explicit SC for: CLAUDE.md update,
  SUB-AGENT-BOUNDARIES.md update, KNOWN-ISSUES.md update (INC-021 reference), legacy
  blackboard/worktree-tracking test file removal/migration.
- Value: FAIL — validation_signal 2. Wants verification mechanisms inline in each SC.
  Suggested SC #1: "verified by simulated two-session collision test demonstrating holder
  notification and no silent dispatch." SC #4: "verified by running two
  /dso:debug-everything sessions in parallel on disjoint bugs and confirming both complete."
- Feasibility: FAIL — technical_feasibility 3, integration_risk 2 (FEASIBILITY_GAP).

## FEASIBILITY_GAP (OPEN — primary reason for pause)

Two unresolved capability gaps requiring multi-machine spike work:

1. Multi-machine git-as-transport CAS coordination unverified for this specific operational
   pattern. Git push CAS primitives (--atomic, --force-with-lease) and fencing-token theory
   are well-documented (GitHub Blog 2015, Kleppmann 2016), but no working examples were found
   of an orphan branch as a coordination bus between multiple machines running AI orchestrators
   with seq-based fencing, INVALIDATION delivery, and tiered evidence-silence timeouts. Spike
   required to validate:
   - CAS round-trip latency under concurrent pushes
   - Non-fast-forward merge behavior with seq-totally-ordered events
   - INVALIDATION signal delivery to in-flight sub-agents in worktrees on remote machines

2. PostToolUse additionalContext reliability for the spec's specific usage:
   - anthropics/claude-code#18427 (Jan 2026): "PostToolUse hooks cannot inject context
     visible to Claude" — known open issue; scope of impact uncertain
   - anthropics/claude-code#24788 (Feb 2026): additionalContext does not surface for MCP
     tool calls — likely doesn't apply since spec uses standard tools, but verify empirically
   Spike required to validate hook injection reliability for: ticket-cli operations, git
   operations, sub-agent dispatch boundaries.

Spike NOT executable in brainstorm session — requires multi-machine setup, network-partition
simulation, real Claude Code orchestrators across machines.

## Outstanding Questions / Decisions Needed on Resume

1. FEASIBILITY_GAP path: spike-ticket-first (a) vs spike-as-first-story-of-Epic-2 (b) vs
   descope-cross-env (c). Last lean: (b) — cross-env is core intent; spike informs subsequent
   story scope; failure replans Epic 2.
2. Apply Value reviewer revisions: add explicit verification mechanism inline in each SC.
3. Apply Scope reviewer revisions: add SC or explicit descoping for CLAUDE.md,
   SUB-AGENT-BOUNDARIES.md, KNOWN-ISSUES.md updates and legacy test cleanup.
4. Re-run Value, Scope, Feasibility reviewers after revisions.
5. SC Gap Check.
6. Approval Gate (AskUserQuestion).
7. On approval: update epic description, file follow-on epics (2b, rolling-batch, RATE_LIMIT),
   write brainstorm:complete tag, classify complexity, route to next skill.

## Web Research Already Completed (don't repeat)

- Distributed claim coordination over Git transports (etcd lease-renewal, Consul session-TTL +
  lock-delay, BullMQ flows, Temporal signals, Kleppmann fencing tokens) — covers Trigger 4
  (novel architectural pattern).
- Sub-agent → orchestrator communication patterns (Temporal signals, Ray actors, Dask, BullMQ,
  Celery, LangGraph interrupts, OpenAI Swarm handoffs, AutoGen GroupChat, GitHub Actions step
  output) — informed terminate-and-escalate decision.

## Process State on Resume

Resume at Step 4 (Fidelity Review) re-run after applying Value + Scope spec revisions and
deciding FEASIBILITY_GAP path. Cross-Epic Interaction Scan (Step 2.25) is complete and need
not be re-run unless substantial scope changes occur.
